steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in the ground beef. Cook and stir until the beef is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Stir in the cabbage, onion, garlic, red pepper flakes, black pepper, and water. Cook and stir until the vegetables are tender, and the water has cooked away, about 10 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the tortillas one at a time in a large skillet over medium heat until pliable.

Place a tortilla onto your work surface, then spoon some of the filling halfway between the bottom edge and the center of the tortilla. Flatten the filling into rectangle shape with the back of a spoon. Sprinkle 1/4 cup of Cheddar cheese over the filling. Fold the bottom of the tortilla snugly over the filling, then fold in the left and right edges. Roll the burrito up to the top edge, forming a tight cylinder. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.

review.reviewBody: This is a variation on a Nebraska staple. In the US we are talking ground round steak which is ground beef. We used to make them with 2 pkg. of Pillsbury Hot Roll Mix, 1 head of cabbage, same ground beef, no red pepper flakes and a little Worcestershire sauce for seasoning. Use a handful of dough, , 1/4 c. filling, pinch the sides, let rise 10 min., and bake on a greased cooked sheet, at 375 for 20 minutes. Just like the ones at the Runza Hut!

I don't give 5 stars often but this deserves it... even though I did change it a little... That being said... Who would have guessed that ground beef and cabbage would make such an awesomely good burrito!?! I changed the recipe slightly... because some people said that the meat can be a little bland, I simmered it in chicken broth instead of water, added a dash of salt and a few dashes of worcestershire sauce. I also added about 1/2 a cup of shredded carrots because I had a small amount that needed using. Quite spicy but if you like heat, these are perfect. How can attest to their deliciousness? My son who loathes veggies ate 2 of these burritos!!!

Just made these for dinner tonight. Excellent recipe, with just a couple small changes. I seasoned the ground beef while it was browning, as some other reviewers recommended, and I added a couple splashes of Worcestershire sauce as well when I added the veggies and water and seasonings. I added chopped green pepper as well with the cabbage and onions, the more veggies the better, I think. Really tasty dinner, even my 7 year old ate it. Thanks!

Very good and different. I left out the red pepper flakes (don't eat anything w/hot spice) and used a bag of cole slaw cabbage since the store I stopped at didn't have any heads of cabbage. It worked out perfect. I added garlic powder and onion powder as someone suggested since I left out the pepper flakes. Husband and I both liked it a lot but he gave it only 4 stars because he said it wasn't as yummy as some of the other recipes I've been making lately. Will be making this again. I know our kids will like it too.

Skipped the tortillas. Served it mixed with brown jasmine rice. Cooked cabbage, onion, and meat (added carrots) in some veggie broth and braggs liquid amino. I cut cheese in half added some sour cream sooo yummy.

Delicious. My six year old who LOVES macaroni & cheese and rates all other meals against it says it's even better than mac & cheese. I was not exact in my measurements and did add steak seasoning in lieu of salt & pepper to add a little pep (while still staying rather true to the recipe.) I also added the shredded cheese to the meat mixture just before putting in the tortillas (for simplicity sake.) Will absolutely make again! Could be an easy go to make ahead meal.

These are really good! And filling! I ended up using more ground round (2 lbs), and 2 medium onions because my half head of cabbage was kind of large. These really came out delicious. My wife really dug it with sour cream, but I ate it naked. Thanks for the awesome recipe!

Have to admit I have never had a Runza before but they sounded yummy (and I needed to use the head of cabbage in my fridge!). I scaled back on the red pepper flakes for the kids, but added some red bell pepper and a bit of shredded carrot, both for taste and a bit of color. It was WONDERFUL!!

These were really good....I added a can of tomato sauce because I thought they might be a little dry and they turned out tasting like cabbage rolls...Anyone who loves cabbage rolls should try that the next time they make these....Yum!

I did not like these at all. It was really easy to make, but that was the only good thing about these burritos. I thought they were extremely bland. I cooked the onions with the ground beef and seasoned the meat with garlic powder, onion powder and red pepper flakes. It still came out really bland. All I could taste was cabbage.....

Alternatives: Crescent rolls, hamburger buns, sauerkraut for cabbage, turkey for beef, chili powder instead of red pepper flakes. Might try mild cannned chopped chili peppers. Since it's a burrito I'd also check out different kinds of salsa, guacamole, sour cream, olives, taco chips or maybe a layered bean dip. Accompaniments might include orange or watermelon with lime juice, or a salad of fruit, a potato or macaroni. or fruit salad. Can't give it 5 stars because red pepper flakes usually aren't to my taste.

I probably screwed it up by shredding the cabbage and onion in a food processor. I cooked it for 2x the length it was supposed to cook for but I still felt the texture was sloppy. I unfortunately did not like the taste and mooshy texture. Shredding vegetables releases WAY too much moisture; I should have just chopped it instead. Also, I added some fresh grated nutmeg which I thought was tasty. And I did like the taste BUT the shredded veggies were just sloshy.
Don't know if I missed something or what, but I added tons of extra spices and these still just didn't do it for us. I really wanted to like these, but we won't make them again. :( Sorry.
Very easy to make and very tasty. Was a hit with my pre-teen girls.
Really good overall. I added more black pepper and some Tony's. Otherrwise, it would have been kinda bland. Also, sharp cheddar is the way to go with these. Good and really easy recipe!
I used ground turkey and served with sour cream and salsa. It sounds strange but is so good! This also makes excellent leftovers.

I really enjoyed this recipe, though I have to say that I only tried it because the ingredients sounded like a strange combination. I tasted the filling and found it a little bland, so I added pepper and garlic powder (not sure how much, just to taste) until I liked the taste. They were so handy to have in the freezer for quick lunches. A definite make again.
Omitted cheese and added a beef bouillon cube.
Awesome! Totally a keeper!
These were very good, and very easy to make. They are fiilling as well. Thanks for sharing. Will make these part of my rotation recipes!
